meta.title: Restore Chrome Bookmarks From a Backup | Snug
meta.description: Restore Chrome bookmarks from an HTML backup with Chrome's import, or with Snug's preview, Merge or Replace, and Undo. Menu paths verified {date}.

title: How do I restore my Chrome bookmarks from a backup?
directAnswer: In Chrome, open {toImportPath} and choose your bookmarks HTML file. Chrome adds the bookmarks to {toImportPlacement}.

builtIn.title: The built-in way
builtIn.intro: Chrome imports a bookmarks HTML file, such as the one you saved when you backed up.
steps: Find the backup file. A Chrome export is named {fromExportFile}.
Choose {toImportSources} as the source and select your file.
Look for the bookmarks in {toImportPlacement}, then move them where you want them.

carriesOver.title: What a restore brings back
carriesOver.intro: A restore brings back the bookmarks the file holds, and only those.
items: Kept in the HTML file, per {fromName}: {fromHtmlKeeps}.
Left out of the HTML file, per {fromName}: {fromHtmlDrops}.
Chrome puts the file's bookmarks in {toImportPlacement}, so bookmarks you already have can appear twice.
The profile file {fromProfileFile} is not an HTML file. Chrome's import lists these sources: {toImportSources}.

withSnug.title: With Snug
withSnug.intro: Snug runs in Chrome. It restores from the files Auto-export saved or from any bookmarks file, and shows a preview before anything changes.
steps: In Chrome, open Snug's Import page and choose the file there, or drop it on the page. Do not use the popup for this: it imports at once, without a preview.
The Preview shows the detected format, the bookmark count and the folder tree before anything changes. Bookmarks that Skip duplicates would leave out are marked.

Choose a mode. Restore — merge places bookmarks in their original locations next to the ones you have. Restore — replace clears your Bookmarks Bar and Other Bookmarks first, then restores the file's bookmarks to their original locations. Both need a file that carries location data.
With Restore — merge you can check single bookmarks or whole folders and import only that selection. Restore — replace always imports everything and takes one file at a time.
Restore — replace shows how many bookmarks it will remove and add, lists the ones it will delete, and asks you to confirm before it runs.
After a replace, click Undo import on the result to put your earlier bookmarks back.
withSnug.snapshot: Before every Restore — replace, Snug saves a Safety snapshot to your Downloads and keeps a copy inside the extension. If the snapshot cannot be saved, nothing is deleted. Settings lists the latest five snapshots, which you can restore or download, and a sixth replaces the oldest. Everything stays on your device and Snug makes no network requests.

goesWrong.title: If something goes wrong
items: You cannot find the bookmarks after Chrome's import. Chrome places them in {toImportPlacement}.
Chrome does not accept the file. Its import lists these sources: {toImportSources}. Check that the file is a bookmarks HTML file.
Restore — replace is unavailable. It needs a file with location data and one file at a time. Use Restore — merge, or Create folder, which works for any file.
You replaced and want your old bookmarks back. Click Undo import, or restore a Safety snapshot in Settings.
Snug says nothing was imported. Every bookmark in the file is already in your browser. Turn off Skip duplicates to import them again.

verified: Menu paths, file names and profile folders were read from {fromName}'s help pages and Chromium's own documents on {date}. Browser menus change between versions, so check the source if a path differs on your screen. Snug's behavior comes from its Importing guide.
